headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channel or write surface is documented, so prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are mostly absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between caveman and godot_rl_agents. caveman has MCP use and file surfaces, but godot_rl_agents exposes no I/O surfaces or ingestion path, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a documented bridge.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents is connected to caveman through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server, reassess upward.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not wire caveman MCP outputs into godot_rl_agents inputs.
Disable any clipboard-based handoff between them.
Review any orchestrator config for hidden shared channels.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but godot_rl_agents lists no data classes touched and both profiles show network egress as none. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, cross-agent leakage is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, reassess upward.
IF godot_rl_agents is configured to ingest caveman files or logs, reassess upward.
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate directories.
Avoid placing sensitive notes in a shared folder.
Confirm both agents remain offline/local-only.
Audit mounts and symlinks for accidental sharing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes to files, while godot_rl_agents exposes no write surfaces or mutable resource scopes. A write-write conflict is not documented; only caveman's side is evidenced. If a shared directory exists, the blast radius is limited to local files, so low is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, reassess upward.
IF godot_rl_agents gains git, filesystem, or database write access, reassess upward.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
Keep godot_rl_agents read-only unless needed.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content, but godot_rl_agents is a game-playing/simulation agent with no documented downstream action authority. There is no evidence that B treats A's output as authoritative by default, so a cascading error chain is not established. Any risk would require an explicit integration not shown here.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes caveman output without verification, reassess upward.
IF caveman output is used to trigger external actions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on caveman outputs.
Do not auto-execute actions from generated text.
Log provenance for any transferred artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. caveman touches local project artifacts, while godot_rl_agents lists no sensitive data classes and no compliance-specific surfaces. Because the profiles do not show a regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, reassess upward.
IF one agent is deployed under stricter retention or residency rules than the other, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Separate environments by jurisdiction if needed.
Review logs for accidental sensitive content.
